what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1994?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 2010 report (calendar wages) and FY2011-FY2025 (fiscal). The 1994 annual town report prints no wage list: its Textract text (lines.tsv, every one of 70 pages) was searched for wage, gross, earnings, payroll and compensation and returned only the Highway narrative (p13 `payroll for the Highway Department`), budget lines (p34 `Compensation Wiring Inspector`, p36 and p43 `Worker's Compensation`, `Unemployment Comp.`), the receipts heading `EARNINGS ON INVESTMENTS` (p32), Article 6's `fix the salaries and compensation of all elected officials` (p42) -- no list by employee (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1994 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 1994?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1994 annual town report prints neither: its text was searched on all 70 pages for salary schedule, classification, grade and step and returned only school grade levels (p12, p22, p25-28) (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the Personnel Bylaw salary schedule and classification plan in force for FY1995, from the Town Clerk or the Personnel Board.

what: What was Lunenburg's fiscal 1994 valuation and tax levy by property class, and what did the overlay and new growth come to?
why: `report-valuation` holds the Assessors' tables (assessments by class, tax history, overlay, new growth) from the 2001-2010 reports and FY2011 onward. The 1994 annual town report prints only two totals on its About the Town page -- `ASSESSED VALUATION: $453,870,017-Real Estate`, `$11,707,235-Personal Property`, `TAX RATE: $15.19 (Fiscal 1994)` (p4) -- and the Board of Assessors' report is narrative (p8); its text was searched on all 70 pages for valuation, assess, tax rate, levy, new growth and overlay and returned no table (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the Town's FY1994 tax rate recapitulation (Form RECAP) and LA-4 as filed with the Division of Local Services.

what: What items made up Lunenburg's FY1995 capital plan, and what did each cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 1994 annual town report prints Article 7 of the May 14, 1994 Annual Town Meeting voting `BORROWING BY EXEMPTION $633,200 FOR CAPITAL EXPENDITURES AS SHOWN ON THE CAPITAL PLAN FOR FY95` (p44) without the plan itself, and the Capital Planning Committee's report names no items or costs (p15: `The Capital Planning Committee will present a Capital Plan for FY'96`); other capital purchases appear as separate warrant articles (p44-p47), several PASSED OVER. Searched for capital plan, capital project, capital outlay and capital expend on all 70 pages (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the FY95 Capital Plan as presented to the May 14, 1994 Annual Town Meeting.

what: What did Lunenburg's capital project funds hold and spend in fiscal 1994?
why: `report-capital-projects` reads the Capital Project Fund statement from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1994 annual town report prints none, and its combined balance sheet has no capital projects column (p31: GENERAL, SPECIAL REVENUE, TRUST and AGENCY, GENERAL LONG-TERM DEBT); article-funded projects appear instead as lines of the general fund appropriations schedule (e.g. p35 `Landfill Closure 2/92 STM`). Whether the town kept a separate capital projects fund in FY1994 is not established. Searched for capital project on all 70 pages: no hit (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the Town's FY1994 audited financial statements (the independent audit, p33 `Annual Audit`) or its FY1994 Schedule A filed with the Division of Local Services.

what: What did Lunenburg owe each year after June 1994, and how much of its debt sat inside the debt limit?
why: `report-debt` holds a debt repayment schedule by issue and fiscal year from the 2001-2010 reports, and `outstanding-debt` the debt-limit split from FY2011 onward. The 1994 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue with fiscal 1995 payments only (p65) and the bonds authorized and unissued (p65); its text was searched on all 70 pages for repayment, schedule of, debt limit, outstanding and indebtedness and returned only p65 and the index entry (p3) (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the Town's FY1994 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1994, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1994 annual town report prints no Inspector of Weights & Measures report: its text was searched for sealer, sealing and weights and returned only the appointment (p6 `INSPECTOR OF WEIGHTS`), the receipts line `SEALING FEES $681.00` (p32), the appropriation line (p34) and the FY95 omnibus line `WEIGHTS /MEASURES` (p43) (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1994 annual report to the Division of Standards.
